cases.name: Two narrative places and historical periods
cases.text: The first part of this novel takes place in Paris, France, in 1808. Louise walks through the streets of Paris to meet the merchant who holds her family’s debt. Her work, courtship and daily life unfold in Paris throughout this part of the story. The second part follows her daughter in London, England, in 1872. She lives and works in London, crosses the Thames each day, and seeks a new life in the city. Both settings shape the characters and their choices.

cases.name: French instruction and Cambridge exam preparation
cases.text: This course teaches French as a second language. Each lesson explains French grammar, French vocabulary and French conversation. Learners practise the French past tense and compare French definite and indefinite articles. A separate English section explicitly prepares students for Cambridge English examinations: exam task formats, timed speaking exercises and practice papers are part of the course. This is instructional preparation for Cambridge English Exams, rather than a history of Cambridge University.

cases.name: Impressionist painting technique
cases.text: This painting manual teaches the Impressionist style. Impressionism captures changing light with broken brushwork and visible strokes. The exercises build Impressionist paintings from patches of color rather than blended studio shading. Every chapter teaches an aspect of Impressionist painting, including complementary colors, open-air observation and fleeting atmospheric effects. Students compare the result with smooth academic painting, then repeat the Impressionist exercise with a new arrangement of light.

cases.text: This cookbook is devoted to Christmas food and Christmas celebrations. The Christmas dinner menu includes roast vegetables, festive breads and a rich fruit pudding. Later chapters describe preparing a Christmas buffet, baking Christmas biscuits and arranging a family Christmas supper. The holiday is the organizing subject of the entire cookbook, rather than an incidental date in a recipe.

cases.name: Ancient Egyptian archaeology and architectural style
cases.text: This archaeological and architectural study covers Ancient Egypt from the Old Kingdom to the end of the pharaonic period, about 2686 BCE to 323 BCE. Its subject is Ancient Egyptian tombs, temples and pyramids, their architecture and their historical development in Ancient Egypt. It examines Ancient Egyptian style: monumental columns, axial temple plans, hieroglyphic decoration and forms tied to Egyptian religious practices. The examples are from ancient Egypt throughout this historical period.
